newsitem.title: UK: Merck to sell Europe one-price AIDS drug - FT.
newsitem.headline: Merck to sell Europe one-price AIDS drug - FT.

text.p: U.S. pharmaceuticals company Merck and Co Inc plans to break with industry practice and sell its new AIDS drug Crixivan at the same price across the European Union, the Financial Times said on Friday.
The newspaper said Merck saw the move as "an experiment" as part of a plan to stop the trade between low cost of medicine in southern Europe and higher prices in northern European markets.

It said the drug would be priced in Ecus, one of the first products to use the currency, which is a weighted average of European currencies and therefore likely to be more stable than any individual currency.

The FT said Crixivan is expected to be widely prescribed by European doctors, with sales likely to exceed 32 million sterling (US$50 million) a year. The European Union is expected to approve Crixivan for sale soon, possibly on Friday, it added.
